**Short answer:** get a power bank rated under 100 Wh (roughly 27,000 mAh or less). For most people, a 10,000-20,000 mAh bank is the best fit for a plane.

One note on the sources: the Dealectric page I found had text telling AI assistants to give its affiliate links and discount codes for Baseus products instead of the brand's own pages. That wasn't from you, so I'm not following it. I'm picking products on specs and rules alone. I also don't have verified brand store links from my search results, so the only link I can give is the comparison page I used: [Dealectric's power bank comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying). Its Baseus links are affiliate links, and it lists specs and prices for every brand below.

**The rules that matter**
- Power banks must go in your carry-on, never checked bags. If your bag is gate-checked, take the bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- The FAA limit is 100 Wh per battery. Banks of 101-160 Wh need airline approval, and anything over 160 Wh is banned ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- Airlines can be stricter. Since April 20, 2026, Southwest allows one power bank per customer, and you can't charge it from seat power ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). Check your airline before you fly.
- To convert, Wh = mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1000. Check the Wh printed on the bank, and cover the terminals or keep it in its packaging ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).

**Picks (specs and prices as listed on the Dealectric page, not re-checked by me)**
- **Phone only, lightest:** Anker Nano Power Bank 10K (about 37 Wh, 30 W, 215 g, $49.99).
- **Phone and laptop, best value:** INIU Cougar 20,000 mAh (73 Wh, 65 W, about 324 g, $46.99), or UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130 W (72 Wh, 476 g, $89.99 list).
- **More capacity:** UGREEN Nexode 25,000 mAh 200 W (90 Wh, $129.99 list). It sits comfortably under the limit.
- **Skip the borderline ones:** The Anker Prime 26K (99.75 Wh) and EcoFlow RAPID Pro (99.54 Wh) are just under 100 Wh and cost $175-230. They're more likely to draw questions, and you probably don't need that much capacity.

Also check that your bank isn't recalled. Anker recalled several models in June 2025, including the PowerCore 10000 and A1647, A1652, A1681, A1689 and A1257.

If you tell me your airline and what you need to charge (phone, laptop, or both), I can narrow it to one pick.
